sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Jérôme Courchesne, Coordinator, Standing Committee, Council and Committee Services, Office of the City Clerk presented the Accessibility Advisory Committee End-of-Term Report 2022-2026 and was available to answer questions from Members of the Advisory Committee.
The Advisory Committee discussed and asked questions regarding the report.

motions.motion_text:
Recommendation(s)
That the Accessibility Advisory Committee approve the End-of-Term Report 2022-2026, and recommend that the Finance and Corporate Services Committee receive the report.

sub_agendas_items.title: Corporate Accessibility Policy Consultation
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Megan Richards, Program Manager, Accessibility, Legislative Services, Office of the City Clerk and Sarah Beriault, Accessibility Specialist, Accessibility Office, Legislative Services, Office of the City Clerk provided a presentation regarding the Corporate Accessibility Policy, consulted Members of the Advisory Committee on proposed changes to the policy, and were available to answer questions from Members. A copy of the slide presentation is filed with the Office of the City Clerk.
The Advisory Committee discussed, asked questions and provided feedback regarding the proposed updates to the Corporate Accessibility Policy.
Following discussion, the Advisory Committee received the presentation.

motions.motion_text:
Recommendation(s)
That the Accessibility Advisory Committee receive the presentation and provide feedback as appropriate.

THAT the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion with regards to establishing clear key performance indicators and associated performance targets for the percentage of e-scooters that are misparked.

sub_agendas_items.title: Motion – Member M. Eliot – Establishing clear key performance indicators and associated performance targets for the percentage of e-scooters that are misparked
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
At the outset, Member Eliot spoke to provide context and then introduced the Motion.
Megan Richards, Program Manager, Accessibility, Legislative Services, Office of the City Clerk and Sarah Beriault, Accessibility Specialist, Accessibility Office, Legislative Services, Office of the City Clerk were present to respond to questions.
Motion No. AAC 2026-35-01 was then put before the Advisory Committee and was subsequently ‘Carried’, as presented.

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS the Accessibility Advisory Committee (AAC) received a presentation from Parking Services on June 16, 2026, regarding the 2025 season results of the Ottawa Shared E-Scooter Program; and
WHEREAS members of the AAC expressed concerns about the continued rate of misparked e-scooters, particularly when they obstruct sidewalks and create barriers for people using mobility devices; and
WHEREAS staff indicated that the program does not currently have key performance indicators (KPIs) that establish an acceptable rate of misparked e-scooters;
BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED THAT the Accessibility Advisory Committee (AAC) recommend that staff establish clear key performance indicators (KPIs) and associated performance targets for the percentage of e-scooters that are misparked, in order to measure the program’s effectiveness in reducing rates of misparking; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the AAC recommend that, in establishing these performance targets, staff consider the sidewalk obstruction rates of other shared mobility programs in other municipalities, including docked bike-share programs; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the AAC recommend that staff consult with the committee in developing these KPIs and performance targets; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the AAC recommend that staff provide the committee with a clearer definition of a “severely misparked” e-scooter that includes e-scooters that obstruct the sidewalk for accessibility devices.
